steps.action: Turn off and unplug the unit. Open the filter door on the back of the unit. Inspect the air filter for dirt or blockage. If dirty, clean per manual: wash in warm water and dishwashing detergent, soak in vinegar solution (1 part vinegar to 3 parts hot water) for 30-45 minutes, rinse thoroughly, and dry completely before reinstalling. Do not operate the unit without the air filter or while the filter is still damp.

cite.quote: 2. Air filter is blocked. 2. Check the air filter.

steps.action: Ensure the unit is positioned at least 6 inches (16 cm) from walls, draperies, or any other objects that might prevent proper airflow. Check the exhaust muffler area (connected to the rotary valve) for obstructions.

cite.quote: 3. Exhaust is blocked. 3. Check the exhaust area; make sure there is nothing restricting the unit exhaust.

steps.action: Verify the flow meter is set to the prescribed flow rate.
steps.expected: Flow meter ball is on the line for the prescribed LPM.

cite.quote: 1. Ensure the flow meter is properly set to the prescribed number.

steps.action: Ensure the patient is on a backup oxygen supply. If cabinet removal is required to access fittings, turn off and unplug the unit, remove cabinets per the manual, then reconnect power with extra care. Apply a certified leak detection solution (must not contain ethylene glycol) to all hose fittings and connections with the unit running. Observe for bubbles indicating leaks. Repair all leaks before returning the unit to service. Do not apply solution to the rotary valve or the PC board assembly.
steps.expected: No signs of leakage (no hissing, no bubbles).

Post-market surveillance for Pure Stationary Oxygen Concentrators model CHSOOO and CHSOOOS
demonstrate an aggregate complaint/service rate greater than 35% for low oxygen purity (output
oxygen below the published specification).
Potential failure of affected units to recharge the battery of the oxygen concentrators.

Breakdown of the sound abatement washer, and metal on metal wear inside the Pressure Equalization (P.E.) valve assembly in the concentrator may lead to failure that can result in self-extinguishing fires or cap explosions.

It was determined that a defective sieve bed subassembly enabled zeolite sieve dust from the sieve beds to migrate into the valves of the manifold assembly and muffler causing a reduction in oxygen concentration.
